title: Introduction to Machine Learning
subtitle: Types of ML, the ML workflow, and when to use ML

content.text: Machine Learning is the field of building systems that learn from data rather than being explicitly programmed. The model finds patterns; you supply the data.

content.definition: Learning from labelled examples: input → known output. Used for classification and regression.
Learning from unlabelled data to find hidden structure, like clustering.
Learning by trial and error with rewards and penalties.

content.code:
# The ML workflow
# 1. Collect & clean data
# 2. Choose a model
# 3. Train (fit) the model
# 4. Evaluate on held-out data
# 5. Tune hyperparameters
# 6. Deploy

from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
print(model.score(X_test, y_test))

questions.question: What is supervised learning?
questions.explanation: Supervised learning uses labelled examples where both input and desired output are known.

faq.q: Do I need a PhD to do ML?
faq.a: No. With Python, scikit-learn, and good data, you can build useful models. Deep learning at scale requires more specialised knowledge.
